#### MATERIAL — F1

> otherwise the turn's own final model text when it is non-empty
- **Question**: specs/verified-completion R1 mandates delivering the turn's final model text whenever it is non-empty, and R3 plus its scenario 'No stub when model text exists' forbid the stub whenever final model text exists — but design D1's preamble exception ('step 2 must not deliver `finalText` on truncated turns') delivers the stub on tool-calls-finish turns that DID produce non-empty (preamble) text. Spec and design mandate different deliverables for the same turn shape; which is authoritative — should the spec carve out tool-calls preamble text, or should the design deliver it? An implementer following the spec literally would leak preambles, and the verify gate would flag the design-compliant implementation non-compliant.
- **Code evidence**: Repo evidence supports the design's behavior, not the spec's text: src/deferred-prompts/proactive-llm-helpers.ts:102-111 (finalizeDeliveryText drops text on finishReason === 'tool-calls' with the comment 'the only text is a preamble, never the answer'); src/llm-orchestrator-send.ts:36-37 (isRisky includes finishReason === 'tool-calls' regardless of text, so preamble-bearing turns reach the builder); src/completion/verified-completion.ts:90 (deriveVerdict 'truncated'); the existing verifier prompt swaps in verifierTruncatedRule for exactly this shape (verified-completion.ts:75-79). The design is code-correct; the delta spec is missing the carve-out, so this is a spec/design reconciliation, not an open product question.
- **Resolution**: edited — specs/verified-completion/spec.md edited: R1 now defines "final model text" to exclude step-capped preamble text (a `tool-calls` finish falls through to the stub, or to verified text when `ok`) and gains the scenario "Step-capped turn does not deliver its preamble"; R3 references the same scoping; R2 carries a preamble-scoping parenthetical. The design's D1 preamble exception is kept unchanged — repo evidence (src/deferred-prompts/proactive-llm-helpers.ts:107-111 finalizeDeliveryText, src/completion/verified-completion.ts:75-79 truncated verifier rule) shows dropping preamble text is the codified behavior, so the spec was reconciled to the design, not vice versa.

- **Code evidence**: src/chat/discord/format-chunking.ts:26-50 read: chunkForDiscord reserves FENCE_CLOSE_LEN/FENCE_OPEN_LEN and, when a chunk ends inside an open fence, prepends a synthetic '```<lang>\n' reopen to the next chunk — concatenating chunks of a fence-spanning reply yields extra fence text beyond boundary whitespace, failing the Content-preservation scenario verbatim. Its own doc comment (lines 12-16) states the preference order "paragraph breaks, then sentence breaks, then word breaks" — sentence/word split points are outside R1's sanctioned order. Wired today at src/chat/discord/reply-helpers.ts:109, src/chat/discord/format.ts:18, src/chat/discord/send-message.ts:41,54; proposal.md Non-goals: "A cross-platform shared formatter or rewrite of Discord chunking."
- **Resolution**: edited — specs/reply-chunking/spec.md R1 now scopes the split-point order and content-preservation rules to the adapters that gain chunking (Telegram, Kontur Talk, Mattermost) and explicitly exempts Discord's frozen splitter — fence rebalancing across chunks and sentence/word break preference are named as permitted, and nothing in the requirement mandates a rewrite of it. #### NITPICK — F3

> THEN the concatenation of the received chunks reproduces the original reply except for whitespace at split boundaries
- **Question**: What is the comparison oracle for "the original reply" on the entity-based platform? Telegram delivers `formatLlmOutput` output — markdown markers become entities, tables are flattened, preprocessLists inflates — so even an unsplit within-limit Telegram message does not byte-reproduce the source markdown. The scenario should name its oracle (e.g., "what an unsplit delivery of the same reply would have delivered"), or an implementer testing against the markdown input fails by construction.
- **Code evidence**: src/chat/telegram/format.ts:151-172,179-193 read: preprocessTables flattens table tokens to plain rows (dropping pipe syntax), preprocessLists inserts blank lines before list items, and markdownToFormattable strips markers into entities — the delivered text is a rewritten form of the markdown. Design D3 confirms chunking splits the markdown and formats each chunk independently, so the concatenation reproduces the formatted delivery, not the source reply. On Mattermost/Kontur Talk (markdown passthrough) and Discord the scenario is literal; only Telegram needs the clarified oracle.
- **Resolution**: edited — The Content-preservation scenario's THEN now names its oracle: concatenation reproduces what an unsplit delivery of the same reply would have delivered — the platform's delivered form (on entity-based Telegram, the formatted delivery rather than the source markdown) — so an implementer testing against the markdown input no longer fails by construction.

#### MATERIAL — F1

> - **THEN** the concatenation of the received chunks reproduces what an unsplit delivery of the same reply would have delivered — the platform's delivered form of the reply (on entity-based Telegram, the formatted delivery rather than the source markdown) — except for whitespace at split boundaries
- **Question**: Should the Content-preservation scenario tolerate formatting-marker artifacts at split points inside spans/fences (mirroring the Discord exemption wording), or should the three adapters balance spans/fences? The spec as written forbids what the design explicitly declines to build — a spec/drafting judgment, but the current text makes the scenario unsatisfiable for inputs R1's own split-point order reaches.

Such splits are reachable under R1's own preference order (a `\n` boundary inside a multi-line bold span; the hard-cut scenario's own example, 'one long unbroken code block', is a mid-fence cut on Telegram), and design.md Risks explicitly accepts the divergence: 'renders as literal backticks or stray `**`/`[` markers but still delivers; fence and span balancing are deliberately out'. Distinct from r2 F3, which fixed which form is the oracle; this is the oracle failing by construction for permitted inputs even after that fix.
- **Resolution**: edited — specs/reply-chunking/spec.md Content-preservation scenario's THEN now exempts formatting markers left unbalanced by a split landing inside an inline span or code fence (they may render literally in adjacent chunks), explicitly declaring span/fence balancing out of scope for the three adapters and mirroring the Discord exemption wording. The scenario is now satisfiable for every split the requirement's own preference order can reach, matching design.md D3's deliberate exclusions and the Risks entry.
